disposition_mapping.rationale: Council convergence (six of seven members) rejected dissolving cutoff enforcement into another step's gating logic: the lock/unlock decision is a discrete, materially consequential, attributable act (KB-03) that a controller or auditor must be able to point to. Checklist distribution and status polling are mechanised, but the go/no-go decision, and an explicit degraded-mode/fallback path for entities without reliable feeds, remain a named human function.

A strong majority (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, emerging_economy, and pragmatist on reconsideration) rejected keeping mechanical and estimation-based journal preparation as internally-labelled tracks within one step, on the grounds that a shared step boundary erodes the IAS 8 accountable-preparer distinction under staffing pressure. The mechanical, template-driven portion becomes straight-through automated posting (TS-02); estimation entries requiring judgment and documented basis retain a named accountable human preparer as a structurally separate step (TS-03), satisfying KB-04/KB-10 and enabling clean actor separation from management review (R2R-R-05).

Allocation running is rule-based computation with no estimation content and no KB entry addressing it directly; council members agreed it belongs alongside mechanical journal posting rather than as a standalone transformation. The one condition preserved from finance_domain/emerging_economy is that allocation-base integrity validation remains a distinct, visible check within the merged step so stale or wrong cost-centre data cannot silently propagate.

Council consensus split matching (high-volume, rule-based, automatable) from mismatch resolution and elimination judgment (inter-entity coordination, cannot be automated). The conflict over whether settlement/elimination postings should be fully straight-through (maximalist) or materiality-gated (agentic_architect, emerging_economy, accounting_standards, hitl_designer) is resolved in favour of gating: postings above a materiality threshold require human release because they are costly to reverse and IFRS 10 completeness (KB-14) depends on eliminations being right, not merely fast. Unresolved mismatches must never be netted into consolidation, preserving elimination completeness.

Risk-tiered automation is adopted for the mechanical matching layer, but the conflict over whether certification itself can be a default system tick is resolved against maximalist's dynamic-erosion model and in favour of hitl_designer/accounting_standards/finance_domain: certification is an attestation act, and for medium/high-risk accounts the human-sign-off floor is fixed by risk rating, not subject to erosion as confidence in tooling grows. Periodic non-exception sampling on auto-certified low-risk accounts is added to address the deskilling/false-quiet risk raised by hitl_designer and emerging_economy. The reconciliation function survives as a distinct, evidence-producing step per R2R-R-01.

Consolidation mechanics (FX retranslation, elimination posting, minority interest) are formulaic given clean inputs and are automated, per the majority view (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) that refusing to automate mechanics does not reduce error risk, it only redirects labour from validation to redundant re-keying. Accounting_standards' sharpening is adopted: exchange differences must be a separately visible, individually labelled output, never netted into a single plug (KB-07/KB-08), and the financial accountant's validation of variances against entity submissions remains a substantive control, not a formality.

The conflict between maximalist's exception-based review and hitl_designer/finance_domain/agentic_architect's insistence on full-result-set visibility with genuine unconstrained investigative authority is resolved in favour of the latter: a controller who only sees a system-curated flagged subset is validating the model's thresholds, not exercising independent judgment, which weakens the last accountable checkpoint before numbers go external. Anomaly detection is retained as decision support only, with no posting or sign-off authority, and actor separation from TS-02/TS-03 is preserved per R2R-R-05/R2R-R-07.

Compilation is automated from signed-off consolidated results, but every council member who addressed this step (hitl_designer, agentic_architect, finance_domain, pragmatist) insisted the last human touch before external/board-facing distribution remain a substantive review, not a distribution trigger. Ordering is enforced as a system gate on TS-06 and TS-08 completion rather than left to calendar convention, satisfying R2R-R-03/R2R-R-04/R2R-R-06.

steps.description: System-driven close calendar and checklist: subledger status (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll) is polled continuously where feeds exist; the checklist with owners and deadlines is generated and tracked automatically with escalation on lateness. Posting lock is proposed by the system on confirmed readiness, but the lock/unlock decision remains a discrete, named go/no-go act by the close manager, not an automated side-effect. Absence, staleness or degradation of a subledger feed is itself treated as an exception requiring escalation (never silently treated as 'ready'), and every entity for which real-time connectivity does not exist retains a defined manual confirmation fallback with a named owner. Every lock/unlock action is logged with a subledger-status snapshot and timestamp.
inputs: Subledger status feeds (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll)
Manual confirmation fallback records for disconnected entities
steps.name: Close orchestration and cutoff control
outputs: Posting locked with logged basis
Checklist tracked with automatic escalation
Data readiness confirmed or exception raised

steps.actor: GL accountant (exception review) with automated posting engine
steps.description: Recurring accruals, prepayment releases per amortisation schedule, routine reclassifications, and cost/overhead allocations (shared-service recharges, corporate overhead, intercompany management fees) are computed and posted straight-through by a rules engine within pre-set tolerance of expected patterns, provided allocation bases and cost-centre data have passed an integrity check. Every automated posting is logged with source-data snapshot, template/model version, threshold applied and timestamp, with an agent identity distinct from human actors. Entries outside tolerance, or allocations with missing/stale/anomalous bases, are routed to the GL accountant, not posted silently. This step does not prepare or post estimation-based entries.
steps.name: Automated mechanical journal and allocation posting
outputs: Mechanical journals and allocation journals posted with full audit trail
Tolerance-breach and base-integrity exceptions routed to GL accountant

steps.description: Provisions, bad-debt and receivables ECL estimates, inventory NRV write-downs, litigation accruals, and judgmental error corrections are prepared by a named, accountable GL accountant with a documented basis and supporting evidence. Models or calculation packs may assist, but a governed model alone is never a sufficient basis; the preparer named on the entry must be able to explain the conclusion. This step is structurally distinct from TS-02 so that mechanical automation can never quietly annex judgment-bearing entries.
steps.name: Estimation and judgment journal preparation
outputs: Estimation-based journals posted with named preparer and documented basis

steps.actor: System matching engine with intercompany specialist oversight
steps.description: High-volume, rule-based matching of intercompany balances (AR/AP mirrors, loans, recharges) runs continuously or in batch across entity pairs, producing a complete per-pair audit trail of matched and unmatched items. For matched balances, settlement, netting and draft elimination entries are generated automatically; postings below a defined materiality threshold execute straight-through with full logging, while settlements and elimination postings above the threshold are gated for human release before execution, because they are costly to reverse and cross entities/currencies. Unmatched items are never netted, force-balanced, or dropped; they are passed to TS-05.
steps.name: Automated intercompany matching and settlement
outputs: Matched balances settled (sub-threshold, straight-through)
Draft settlements/eliminations above threshold gated for release
Unmatched items escalated with audit trail

steps.description: Genuine mismatches escalated from TS-04 are investigated and resolved through coordination with counterparty entities, requiring judgment that automation cannot substitute for. Resolved items feed elimination-entry preparation for consolidation; unresolved items are aged and tracked but must never enter consolidation as a netted or suppressed adjustment. This step and its completion are a precondition for consolidation eliminations to be treated as final.
steps.name: Intercompany mismatch resolution and elimination preparation
outputs: Mismatches resolved or explicitly flagged unresolved
Elimination entries prepared and traceable to resolved matches

steps.description: Reconciliation against subledgers, bank statements and supporting schedules runs via an automated matching/evidence-assembly engine for all accounts per the reconciliation policy. Low-risk, high-volume accounts within tolerance auto-certify, but are subject to periodic non-exception sampling by GL accountants to preserve reviewer calibration and to catch feed-quality failures the engine cannot see. Medium- and high-risk-rated accounts retain the full manual certification-with-evidence discipline: certification is an attestation act that must always terminate in a named, accountable human sign-off for this population, regardless of automation maturity — this floor is fixed by risk rating and is not eroded by confidence in tooling. Unreconciled items are flagged, aged and escalated with a defined path to resolution; aging is never a permanent resting state.
steps.name: Risk-tiered reconciliation and certification
outputs: Auto-certifications for low-risk accounts with sampled human review
Human certifications with evidence for medium/high-risk accounts
Unreconciled items flagged, aged and tracked to resolution

steps.description: An automated consolidation engine prepares the trial balance roll-up, retranslates monetary items at the closing rate, computes exchange differences as a separately visible, individually labelled output (never netted into a single consolidation plug), posts intercompany eliminations sourced from TS-05, and calculates minority interest. The financial accountant validates completeness and investigates flagged variances against entity submissions before results pass to management review; any change to translation, elimination, or minority-interest computation methodology is surfaced for disclosure rather than silently absorbed.
steps.name: Consolidation and FX translation
outputs: Consolidated balances with FX translation and exchange differences separately visible
Variance exceptions validated
Methodology changes surfaced for disclosure

steps.description: The controller reviews the full draft consolidated result set — not a system-curated subset — with an anomaly-detection capability providing decision support by ranking variances against expectations and prior period; the controller retains unrestricted authority to investigate anywhere in the result set, not only flagged items. The controller investigates anomalies, determines, documents and posts management adjustments, and signs off account-level results. This actor must be distinct from the preparers in TS-02 and TS-03.
steps.name: Management review and adjustments
outputs: Management adjustments posted
Account-level sign-off with full-visibility review evidenced

steps.description: Compilation of financial statements, variance schedules and KPI summaries is drafted automatically from signed-off consolidated results, including draft management commentary. A human (group reporting accountant, with controller co-sign for external/board-facing content) performs a substantive review and approval before distribution; auto-compile-and-auto-send is not permitted. System-enforced gating requires TS-06 (reconciliation) and TS-08 (management review) to be complete before this step can execute, and distribution mechanics degrade gracefully for recipients without high-bandwidth reporting platforms.
steps.name: Financial reporting package
outputs: Reporting package reviewed, approved and distributed
